# Quantitative reference points

Use these instead of adjectives. Every number below is sourced.

| Metric | Value | Context | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum body font size | 10 pt (bare minimum; often larger depending on typeface) | Stonemaier Games house practice | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Recommended 'clear print' font size | 12 pt minimum; 16 pt Arial+ for large-print editions | General accessibility guidance | [Rulebook Design: Contrast and Readability – MINIFINITI](https://minifiniti.com/blogs/game-talk/rulebook-design-contrast-and-readability) |
| Dyslexia-friendly font size | 12-14 pt, line-height >= 1.5x | Dyslexia style guidance | [Rulebook Design: Contrast and Readability – MINIFINITI](https://minifiniti.com/blogs/game-talk/rulebook-design-contrast-and-readability) |
| Text contrast ratio | 4.5:1 normal text; 3:1 large or bold text (18pt / 14pt bold) | WCAG-derived | [Rulebook Design: Contrast and Readability – MINIFINITI](https://minifiniti.com/blogs/game-talk/rulebook-design-contrast-and-readability) |
| Colour vision deficiency prevalence | ~8% of men, ~0.5% of women; ~300 million people worldwide | Accessibility rationale | [Rulebook Design: Contrast and Readability – MINIFINITI](https://minifiniti.com/blogs/game-talk/rulebook-design-contrast-and-readability) |
| Preferred rulebook trim size | 180 x 240 mm | Stonemaier: big enough for visuals, small enough to leave on the table | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Page count constraint | Must be divisible by 4 (spreads) | Print binding reality | [Resonym | Writing Rulebooks](https://resonym.com/writing-rulebooks/) |
| Extra pages to budget when self-publishing | 2-4 more than you think you need | Easier to fill space than to create it after layout | [Resonym | Writing Rulebooks](https://resonym.com/writing-rulebooks/) |
| Freelance rules editor rate (2020 survey range) | USD 25-50 / hour for most editors; more for the very experienced | Meeple Mountain | [Top Six Rules for Rulebook Writing – Meeple Mountain](https://www.meeplemountain.com/top-six/top-six-rules-for-writing-rulebooks/) |
| Editor error-catch rate | 80-95% per pass — hence editor + separate proofreader | The Copyeditor's Handbook, cited by Curby | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| Rewrites to expect | Write it, then rewrite twice; the third draft is materially better | BGG designer rule of thumb | [BGG: how to write rule book](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2040012/how-to-write-rule-book) |
| Blind playtests recommended | At least 1; 2-3 for medium-to-heavy games | Meeple Mountain | [Top Six Rules for Rulebook Writing – Meeple Mountain](https://www.meeplemountain.com/top-six/top-six-rules-for-writing-rulebooks/) |
| Share of blind playtesting aimed at the rulebook | ~25% | Stonemaier | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Rulebooks edited by a single career rules editor | 100+ titles (Michael Lee); ~100 rulebooks (Paul Grogan) | Evidence that this is a profession | [Michael Lee, Editor — editing.curby.net](https://editing.curby.net/) |
| Style guide length benchmark | ~13,000 words (Curby's free board game editing style guide) | Free, CC-licensed | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| Rules-question volume as a quality proxy | 1,500+ BGG rules threads for one first-printing card game | Pathfinder ACG: Rise of the Runelords | [BGG: Worst rulebook ever!](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1554960/worst-rulebook-ever) |
